name: Shichi Narabe
description: Shichi Narabe is a Japanese layout shedding game related to Fan Tan/Sevens. Players lay out all sevens first, then extend each suit outward toward Ace and King while managing a limited number of passes.

overview.description: Shichi Narabe is a Japanese layout shedding game related to Fan Tan/Sevens. Players lay out all sevens first, then extend each suit outward toward Ace and King while managing a limited number of passes.

history.origins: Shichi Narabe is the Japanese form of Sevens/Fan Tan, adapted with explicit passing limits and several local tactical variants.
timeline: Traditional period: Sevens-style layout play circulates in Japan under the name Shichi Narabe.
Modern era: Variant families (Joker, Tunnel, Ghost, Killing) become widely documented.
Current era: Online implementations spread standardized and house-rule versions.
history.cultural: Common as a social table game and often taught as an accessible strategic card game.
history.evolution: Japanese rules introduced pass-economy pressure and special variants that punish blocking more strongly than many Western Sevens forms.

setup.players: 3 or more players; 3-5 is commonly preferred.
setup.deck: Use a standard 52-card deck; add one Joker for the Joker variant.
setup.dealing: Deal all cards one-by-one clockwise. All players who hold sevens place them face up to start the layout.
setup.equipment: Cards and table space for a 13x4 suit layout.

rules.objective: Empty your hand as early as possible while avoiding bankruptcy from overusing passes.
rules.gameplay: The player associated with the seven of diamonds starts, then play continues clockwise. On a turn, play one legal adjacent rank in a suit row or pass. Legal plays extend each suit outward from 7 toward K and A. Each player may pass at most three times; a player who must pass again while still holding cards goes bankrupt and is ranked behind active finishers.
keyRules: All sevens are laid out before normal turns begin.
Each player has a strict pass limit (typically three).
Finishing order determines ranking; bankrupt players are last.

strategy.basic: Avoid spending passes too early unless doing so meaningfully blocks opponents' key exits.
strategy.intermediate: Control choke cards near 7s to force opponents into pass pressure.
strategy.advanced: Time releases of blocked suit branches to avoid becoming the final trapped holder.
tips: Track each player's remaining passes as a primary tempo resource.
Do not over-block if it leaves you with isolated high/low cards at endgame.

variations.name: Joker Variant
variations.description: Adds a Joker with exchange mechanics that can skip blocked cards in a row.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Joker exchange and skip-block rules are not yet mapped to engine constants.

variations.name: Tunnelling
variations.description: Suit row ends connect so completion can force reverse-order continuation.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Tunnel wrap and reverse-order rules need engine support before overrides.

scoring.description: No fixed point values in the base game; results are by finishing order, with bankrupt players ranked behind finishers.
scoring.winCondition: Finish your hand before opponents; avoid bankruptcy from a fourth forced pass.

synthesis.shortDescription: Shichi Narabe is Japan's strategic Sevens variant where pass limits and layout blocking create tactical pressure in a simple play-one-card-or-pass loop.

hero.title: SHICHI NARABE
hero.subtitle: Layout Shedding Game
hero.tagline: Build out from sevens, manage your three passes, and empty your hand first.
